items.title: Finite-range Dobrushin uniqueness and boundary influence
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice, $d\geq1$, a finite nonempty alphabet $A$, and a proper, consistent finite-range specification $\gamma$ on $X=A^{\mathbb Z^d}$ with its cylinder-generated Borel $\sigma$-algebra, using [[def-csm-lattice-gibbs-specification]]. Here consistency means $\gamma_\Lambda\gamma_\Delta=\gamma_\Lambda$ for finite $\Delta\subseteq\Lambda$, properness means $\gamma_\Lambda(r_\Lambda^{-1}(D)\mid\eta)=\mathbf1_D(\eta)$ for each exterior-measurable event $D\subseteq A^{\Lambda^c}$ and $\eta\in A^{\Lambda^c}$, where $r_\Lambda:X\to A^{\Lambda^c}$ is coordinate restriction; in compositions and integrals against measures on $X$, every kernel takes the appropriate exterior restriction of the global configuration as its argument, and finite range means each $\gamma_\Delta(\mathbf1_C\mid\cdot)$ for finite $\Delta$ and cylinder event $C$ depends on only finitely many exterior coordinates. Also assume a uniform finite integer radius $R\geq0$ such that each one-site kernel $\gamma_{\{i\}}$ depends only on exterior spins $j$ with $\|i-j\|_\infty\leq R$. For each pair of sites define $c_{ij}$ as the supremum of the half-total-variation change in the one-site conditional law at $i$ when only exterior spin $j$ is changed, where half-total variation for probability vectors $p,q$ on $A$ is $\frac12\sum_{a\in A}|p(a)-q(a)|$, and set $c_{ii}=0$. If
$$c=\sup_i\sum_jc_{ij}<1,$$
then the DLR state is unique. Moreover, for a finite region $\Lambda$ and two exterior conditions $\xi,\zeta$, couple the random-scan finite-volume heat-bath chains by choosing the same uniformly random site and using a maximal coupling of its two single-site conditional laws. A stationary joint law of this pair chain exists. If the distance $\operatorname{dist}_\infty(i,\Lambda^c):=\inf_{j\notin\Lambda}\|i-j\|_\infty$ is at least $r(R+1)$ for a nonnegative integer $r$, then its disagreement probability at $i$ is at most $c^r/(1-c)$. Consequently every local conditional expectation becomes uniformly insensitive to boundary conditions as $\Lambda\uparrow\mathbb Z^d$.

items.title: Ising influence bounded by hyperbolic tangent
items.statement:
Let $d\geq1$, let spins be $s_i\in\{-1,+1\}$, let $h_i\in\mathbb R$, and let $J_{ij}=J_{ji}\in\mathbb R$ with $J_{ii}=0$ and $J_{ij}=0$ whenever $\|i-j\|_\infty>R$ for some finite integer $R$. No translation invariance is assumed. For finite $\Lambda\subset\mathbb Z^d$ and exterior $\eta\in\{-1,+1\}^{\Lambda^c}$, define $\widehat s_i=s_i$ on $\Lambda$ and $\widehat s_i=\eta_i$ outside, and use
$$E_\Lambda(s_\Lambda\mid\eta)=-\sum_{\{i,j\}:\{i,j\}\cap\Lambda\ne\varnothing}J_{ij}\widehat s_i\widehat s_j-\sum_{i\in\Lambda}h_i s_i,$$
where the pair sum is over unordered distinct pairs and is finite by the range assumption. For site $i$ and exterior spins $\eta\in\{-1,+1\}^{\mathbb Z^d\setminus\{i\}}$, the one-site law is explicitly
$$\gamma_i(s\mid\eta)=\frac{\exp\!\left(\beta\left[h_i s+\sum_{k\ne i}J_{ik}s\eta_k\right]\right)}{\sum_{u\in\{-1,+1\}}\exp\!\left(\beta\left[h_i u+\sum_{k\ne i}J_{ik}u\eta_k\right]\right)},\qquad s\in\{-1,+1\};$$
the sums are finite by the range condition. For $i\ne j$, define
$$c_{ij}:=\sup_{\eta,\eta':\,\eta_k=\eta'_k\ (k\ne j)}\frac12\sum_{s\in\{-1,+1\}}|\gamma_i(s\mid\eta)-\gamma_i(s\mid\eta')|,\qquad c_{ii}:=0.$$
Then $c_{ij}=0$ if $J_{ij}=0$, and otherwise
$$c_{ij}\leq\tanh(\beta|J_{ij}|).$$
In particular, $\sup_i\sum_j\tanh(\beta|J_{ij}|)<1$ is a sufficient Dobrushin row-sum bound for every bounded field profile $(h_i)$.

items.title: Unique interacting Ising state at sufficient high temperature
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice, spins $s_i\in\{-1,+1\}$, inverse temperature $\beta>0$, a constant finite field $h\in\mathbb R$, and symmetric pair couplings with zero diagonal, $J_{ij}=J_{ji}$ and $J_{ii}=0$, satisfying $J_{i+k,j+k}=J_{ij}$ for all $i,j,k\in\mathbb Z^d$, and $J_{ij}=0$ when $\|i-j\|_\infty>R$ for some finite integer $R\geq0$. For finite $\Lambda$, use the conditional energy
$$E_\Lambda(s_\Lambda\mid\eta)=-\sum_{\{i,j\}:\{i,j\}\cap\Lambda\ne\varnothing}J_{ij}\widehat s_i\widehat s_j-h\sum_{i\in\Lambda}s_i,$$
where $\widehat s_i=s_i$ on $\Lambda$ and $\widehat s_i=\eta_i$ outside; let $\gamma$ be the corresponding finite-alphabet Gibbs specification from [[def-csm-lattice-gibbs-specification]]. If
$$\sup_i\sum_j\tanh(\beta|J_{ij}|)<1,$$
then there exists exactly one DLR state. For homogeneous nearest-neighbor coupling $J$ this sufficient condition is $2d\tanh(\beta|J|)<1$. It is not asserted to be sharp.

items.title: Bounded lattice pressure on van Hove sets
items.statement:
Let $d\geq1$, $A$ be finite nonempty, and let a bounded translation-invariant finite-range interaction on $A^{\mathbb Z^d}$ be as in [[def-csm-finite-range-lattice-interaction]]. Fix $\beta>0$, set $C_L=\{1,\ldots,L\}^d$ for each integer $L\geq1$, and define $Z_L=\sum_{\sigma\in A^{C_L}}e^{-\beta H_{C_L}^{\rm free}(\sigma)}$ and $p_L=|C_L|^{-1}\log Z_L$. For a van Hove sequence of finite sets $\Lambda_n\subset\mathbb Z^d$, meaning $|\Lambda_n|\to\infty$ and $|\{x\in\Lambda_n:\operatorname{dist}_\infty(x,\Lambda_n^c)\leq r\}|/|\Lambda_n|\to0$ for every fixed $r$, the free-boundary pressure
$$p_{\Lambda_n}=\frac{1}{|\Lambda_n|}\log\sum_{\sigma\in A^{\Lambda_n}}e^{-\beta H_{\Lambda_n}^{\rm free}(\sigma)}$$
and the cubic sequence $p_L$ both converge to the same finite limit $p$. Bounded finite-range interactions are essential; this statement does not concern continuum particles or long-range models.

items.title: Stationary lattice entropy and energy densities
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and let $A$ be finite nonempty. A consistent translation-stationary family means probability measures $\nu_F$ on $A^F$ for every finite $F\subset\mathbb Z^d$, with $\nu_E=(\pi_E^F)_*\nu_F$ whenever $E\subseteq F$ and $\nu_{F+j}=(\tau_j)_*\nu_F$ for every $j\in\mathbb Z^d$, where $(\pi_E^F x)=x|_E$ and $(\tau_jx)_{i+j}=x_i$. This family extends to a unique translation-stationary probability $\mu$ on the cylinder sigma-algebra. Set $B_n=[-n,n]^d\cap\mathbb Z^d$ for each integer $n\geq1$. For any such stationary $\mu$ and any bounded translation-invariant finite-range interaction $(\mathcal R,(S_r,\Phi_r)_{r\in\mathcal R})$ as in [[def-csm-finite-range-lattice-interaction]], define
$H_n=-\sum_{\sigma\in A^{B_n}}\mu_{B_n}(\sigma)\log\mu_{B_n}(\sigma)$ with $0\log0=0$, and
$u(\mu)=\sum_{r\in\mathcal R}\sum_{a\in A^{S_r}}\mu(\sigma|_{S_r}=a)\Phi_r(a)$.
Then
$$h(\mu)=\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{H_n}{|B_n|}=\inf_{\ell\geq1}\frac{H_\ell}{|B_\ell|}$$
exists in $[0,\log|A|]$, and the free-boundary interaction-energy density satisfies
$$\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{\mathbb E_\mu[H^{\rm free}_{B_n}]}{|B_n|}=u(\mu).$$

items.title: DLR states attain the bounded lattice pressure variational principle
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice, a bounded translation-invariant finite-range lattice interaction on a finite alphabet, and $\beta>0$. Let $p$ be its dimensionless pressure per site, and let $\mu$ be a translation-stationary probability with entropy density $h(\mu)$ and energy density $u(\mu)$ as in [[lem-csm-stationary-lattice-entropy-energy]]. Then
$$h(\mu)-\beta u(\mu)\leq p.$$
If $\mu$ is a DLR state for the specification, equality holds. Since stationary DLR states exist under these hypotheses, the supremum of $h(\mu)-\beta u(\mu)$ over stationary probabilities is attained and equals $p$. The converse “every maximizing stationary probability is DLR” is not asserted.

items.title: Peierls contour probability bound
items.statement:
Let $n\in\mathbb Z_{\geq0}$ and $B_n=[-n,n]^2\cap\mathbb Z^2$. For $s\in\{-1,+1\}^{B_n}$, set $\widehat s_i=s_i$ for $i\in B_n$ and $\widehat s_i=+1$ for $i\notin B_n$, and define
$$H_{B_n}^+(s)=-J\sum_{\substack{\{i,j\}\subset\mathbb Z^2:\ |i-j|_1=1,\ \{i,j\}\cap B_n\ne\varnothing}}\widehat s_i\widehat s_j,\qquad Z_{B_n}^+=\sum_{s\in\{-1,+1\}^{B_n}}e^{-\beta H_{B_n}^+(s)},\qquad \gamma_{B_n}^+(s)=(Z_{B_n}^+)^{-1}e^{-\beta H_{B_n}^+(s)}.$$
The energy sum is finite because $B_n$ is finite and interactions are nearest-neighbor. For the nearest-neighbor Ising model with coupling $J>0$, zero field and $\beta>0$, any simple dual cycle $\gamma$ that occurs in the disagreement graph of a configuration determines the event $A_\gamma$ that all primal bonds crossed by $\gamma$ have disagreeing spins. Then
$$\gamma_{B_n}^+(A_\gamma)\leq e^{-2\beta J|\gamma|}.$$
For each such cycle, the parity-inside is defined by [[lem-csm-ising-parity-contours]] and lies in the variable box.

items.title: Two-dimensional Ising Gibbs coexistence at low temperature
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. For the nearest-neighbor ferromagnetic Ising model on $\mathbb Z^2$ with coupling $J>0$, zero field, and $\beta J\geq2$, there exist two distinct translation-stationary DLR states $\mu_+$ and $\mu_-$ such that for every site $i$,
$$\mu_+(s_i)\geq m_*>0,\qquad \mu_-(s_i)\leq-m_*.$$
One may take $m_*=1-2\delta(\beta J)$, where
$$\delta(K)=\frac43\,\frac{r^4(5-4r)}{(1-r)^2},\qquad r=3e^{-2K}.$$
This is a sufficient low-temperature bound; the states are not asserted to be extremal and $K=2$ is not claimed to be critical.

items.title: Coexistence implies an Ising pressure cusp
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and fix $\beta>0$ and $J>0$ with $\beta J\geq2$. For $B_n=[-n,n]^2\cap\mathbb Z^2$, define the free-boundary field-dependent energy and partition function by
$$H_{B_n}^{(h),\mathrm{free}}(s)=-J\sum_{\substack{x\in B_n,\ k\in\{1,2\}:\\x+e_k\in B_n}}s_xs_{x+e_k}-h\sum_{x\in B_n}s_x,\qquad Z_n(h)=\sum_{s\in\{-1,+1\}^{B_n}}e^{-\beta H_{B_n}^{(h),\mathrm{free}}(s)}.$$
The bounded finite-range pressure theorem gives the finite limit $p(h):=\lim_{n\to\infty}|B_n|^{-1}\log Z_n(h)$ for each $h\in\mathbb R$. Here $h$ is the field energy per spin, while $h_{\rm Sh}(\mu)$ below denotes Shannon entropy per site. The dimensionless pressure $p(h)$ is not differentiable at $h=0$. More precisely, if the stationary DLR states at zero field have magnetizations at least $m_*>0$ and at most $-m_*$, then every positive-field secant slope from zero is at least $\beta m_*$ and every negative-field secant slope is at most $-\beta m_*$. This proves a sufficient coexistence cusp; it does not identify the critical coupling.

items.title: Exact convergent Ising-chain high-temperature series
items.statement:
For the zero-field nearest-neighbor Ising chain with spins $s_i\in\{-1,+1\}$, coupling $J\in\mathbb R$, inverse temperature $\beta>0$, and $K=\beta J$, let $P(K)$ be the dimensionless pressure per site on periodic chains. For $|K|<\tfrac12$,
$$P(K)=\log(2\cosh K)=\log2+\sum_{m=1}^{\infty}\frac{(-1)^{m+1}}{m}(\cosh K-1)^m.$$
The series converges absolutely at every such $K$ and uniformly on each compact subinterval of $(-\tfrac12,\tfrac12)$. This is a sufficient convergence range for this specific one-dimensional model, not a generic cluster-expansion result.

items.title: Positive Ising transfer matrix and stationary Markov law
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. For finite $\beta>0$ and $J,h\in\mathbb R$, set $K=\beta J$, $b=\beta h$, and define the positive symmetric transfer matrix on $\{-1,+1\}$ by
$$T_{s,t}=e^{Kst+b(s+t)/2}.$$
Let $\lambda_+$ be its larger eigenvalue and let $r$ be its strictly positive unit eigenvector, with coordinates $r_s$. Then
$$Q_{s,t}=\frac{T_{s,t}r_t}{\lambda_+r_s},\qquad \pi_s=r_s^2$$
define a stochastic matrix $Q$ and invariant probability vector $\pi$. Their consistent consecutive-block laws $\pi_{s_\ell}\prod_{i=\ell}^{r-1}Q_{s_i,s_{i+1}}$ extend uniquely to a stationary probability measure on $\{-1,+1\}^{\mathbb Z}$.

items.title: Conditional Ising equilibrium phase predictions
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice and adopt [[post-csm-interacting-equilibrium-gibbs]] for the specified classical Ising model. In the SI interpretation of [[def-csm-gibbs-physical-parameters]], $\beta=(k_BT)^{-1}$ is in $\mathrm{J}^{-1}$, $J$ is the coupling energy $J_{\rm I}$ in joules, and $h$ is an energy bias per dimensionless spin in joules, not a magnetic-field strength; hence $\beta J$ and $\beta h$ are dimensionless. The conditional model predictions are: (i) for a one-dimensional nearest-neighbor chain with finite $\beta>0$, $J,h\in\mathbb R$, the DLR equilibrium state is unique; (ii) for a translation-invariant finite-range Ising pair interaction with symmetric zero-diagonal couplings $J_{ij}=J_{ji}$, $J_{ii}=0$ and constant finite field, the sufficient condition $\sup_i\sum_j\tanh(\beta|J_{ij}|)<1$ gives a unique DLR equilibrium state; and (iii) for the two-dimensional nearest-neighbor ferromagnet at $h=0$ and $\beta J\geq2$, there are distinct stationary DLR equilibrium states with opposite nonzero magnetization and the pressure is nondifferentiable in $h$ at zero. These deductions are restricted to the stated classical model; they do not report a measured transition or infer a phase diagram between the sufficient regimes.
items.physical_scope: Classical translation-invariant finite-range Ising pair models on Z^d, d>=1, under the stated sufficient uniqueness condition; finite-temperature nearest-neighbor chains; and zero-field two-dimensional nearest-neighbor ferromagnets with J>0 and beta J>=2 for coexistence and the pressure cusp. Conditional model predictions only; no measured critical point or universal phase diagram.

items.title: Gibbs pressure and entropy with physical reference units
items.statement:
Assume the adopted interacting Gibbs-equilibrium postulate for a bounded finite-range translation-invariant lattice model in dimension $d\geq1$, Countable Choice, lattice spacing $a>0$ metres, and temperature $T>0$ kelvin. For any stationary DLR equilibrium state with dimensionless pressure per site $p$, Shannon entropy density $h_{\rm Sh}$ in nats per site, and mean energy $u$ in joules per site, the conditional model prediction is
$$\mathsf P=\frac{k_BT}{a^d}p,\qquad s=\frac{k_B}{a^d}h_{\rm Sh},\qquad f=\frac{u}{a^d}-Ts=-\frac{k_BT}{a^d}p.$$
The generalized pressure density $\mathsf P$ and free-energy density $f$ have units $\mathrm{J\,m}^{-d}$; for $d=3$, $\mathsf P$ is in pascals ($\mathrm{Pa}=\mathrm{J\,m}^{-3}$). The reference spin entropy density $s$ has units $\mathrm{J\,K}^{-1}\mathrm{m}^{-d}$. This is a consequence of the bounded-lattice DLR variational identity; it makes no claim that the model describes a material.
items.physical_scope: Bounded finite-alphabet translation-invariant finite-range lattice models under the stated DLR and SI reference conventions; conditional model deductions only.

row.title: Finite-range continuum Gibbs kernels and DLR notion

items.title: Finite-range continuum Gibbs kernels and DLR notion
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice [[def-axiom-of-choice]] and fix an integer dimension $d\geq1$. A configuration is a locally finite simple point set $\omega\subset\mathbb R^d$ with the count sigma-algebra and unit-intensity Poisson reference from [[def-tdmath-poisson-configuration-reference]]; thus every bounded Borel set contains finitely many points, and the sigma-algebra is generated by its bounded-set counts. Write $N_A(\omega)=|\omega\cap A|$.

Use the interface of [[def-csm-stable-superstable-continuum-interaction]]: $\phi:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}$ is even and Borel, and some finite $B\geq0$ satisfies $U_N(X)\geq-BN$ for every finite position list $X=(x_1,\ldots,x_N)$. For a finite simple configuration $\omega$, enumerate its points as such a list and write $U_\phi(\omega)=\sum_{\{x,y\}\subset\omega}\phi(x-y)$; its unordered-pair arguments are nonzero, and stability gives $U_\phi(\omega)\geq-B|\omega|$. For this item assume finite range $R>0$, meaning $\phi(x)=0$ whenever $\|x\|_2>R$.

Let $\Lambda\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a nonempty bounded Borel region and let $\eta\subset\Lambda^c$ be a locally finite exterior configuration. The relevant exterior set is
$$\eta_\Lambda^R=\{y\in\eta:\operatorname{dist}_2(y,\Lambda)\leq R\};$$
it is finite because it lies in a bounded set. For a finite interior configuration $\omega\subset\Lambda$, define the conditional energy
$$H_\Lambda(\omega\mid\eta)=\sum_{\{x,y\}\subset\omega}\phi(x-y)+\sum_{x\in\omega}\sum_{y\in\eta_\Lambda^R}\phi(x-y).$$
For positive mathematical parameters $z,\beta>0$, define the unit-Poisson-reference partition integral and candidate kernel by
$$Z_\Lambda^\eta(z,\beta)=\int z^{N_\Lambda(\omega)}e^{-\beta H_\Lambda(\omega\mid\eta)}\,Q_\Lambda(d\omega),\qquad \gamma_\Lambda^\eta(d\omega)=\frac{z^{N_\Lambda(\omega)}e^{-\beta H_\Lambda(\omega\mid\eta)}}{Z_\Lambda^\eta(z,\beta)}\,Q_\Lambda(d\omega),$$
where $Q_\Lambda$ is the restriction of the unit-intensity Poisson law and $e^{-\beta(+\infty)}=0$. The accompanying lemma proves that $Z_\Lambda^\eta$ is finite and strictly positive and that $\eta\mapsto\gamma_\Lambda^\eta$ is a probability kernel.

Extend $\gamma_\Lambda^\eta$ to a kernel on full configurations by replacing the interior with $\omega$ and leaving $\eta$ unchanged outside $\Lambda$. A continuum DLR law for this specification is a probability measure $\mu$ on configuration space satisfying $\mu\gamma_\Lambda=\mu$ for every nonempty bounded Borel $\Lambda$, where this identity means equality of integrals for every bounded measurable full-configuration test. The kernel consistency and its conditional-law interpretation are proved in [[lem-csm-continuum-kernel-normalization]]. This definition asserts no existence, uniqueness, or thermodynamic-limit result.

items.title: Stable finite-range continuum specification normalization and consistency
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and fix $d\geq1$. For every bounded Borel set $D\subset\mathbb R^d$ and $n\in\mathbb N_0$, the unit-intensity Poisson law restricted to $N_D=n$, represented on ordered simple tuples in $D^n$ before forgetting labels, is the pushforward of $e^{-|D|}/n!$ times product Lebesgue measure. Now fix a nonempty bounded Borel region $\Lambda\subset\mathbb R^d$, a stable even Borel pair potential $\phi$ with finite range $R>0$ as in [[def-csm-continuum-dlr-kernels]], a locally finite exterior configuration $\eta\subset\Lambda^c$, and $z,\beta>0$. Let $m=N_{\Lambda^R}(\eta)$, with $\Lambda^R=\{y:\operatorname{dist}_2(y,\Lambda)\leq R\}$. Then the partition integral in [[def-csm-continuum-dlr-kernels]] obeys
$$e^{-|\Lambda|}\leq Z_\Lambda^\eta(z,\beta)\leq e^{-|\Lambda|}\exp\!\left(z|\Lambda|e^{\beta B(1+2m)}\right)<\infty.$$
Consequently $\gamma_\Lambda^\eta$ is a Borel probability kernel in $\eta$. For every nonempty bounded Borel region $\Delta\subseteq\Lambda$, the extended kernels satisfy $\gamma_\Lambda\gamma_\Delta=\gamma_\Lambda$, and their fixed measures are exactly the probability laws whose conditional distribution inside each $\Lambda$, given the exterior, is $\gamma_\Lambda^\eta$.

items.title: Qualified interacting continuum thermodynamic and positional ensemble limits
items.statement:
For clauses 1–7 assume the adopted classical Gibbs-equilibrium postulate and parameter conventions of [[post-csm-interacting-equilibrium-gibbs]] and [[def-csm-gibbs-physical-parameters]], with a single positional species and reference exactly matching the mathematical suppliers below. Use the postulate’s thermal-wavelength convention with reference-action identification $a_0=h_{\rm ref}$ and its operationally indistinguishable $1/N!$ sector factor. Let $d\geq1$. Fix a reference length $\ell_0>0$ in metres and energy scale $E_0>0$ in joules. If the physical inverse temperature is $\beta_{\rm SI}=(k_BT)^{-1}>0$ in J$^{-1}$ and physical activity is $z_c>0$ in m$^{-d}$ as defined in [[def-csm-gibbs-physical-parameters]], the numerical mathematical inputs are $\beta=E_0\beta_{\rm SI}$ and $z=\ell_0^d z_c$; coordinates and pair energies are expressed in units $\ell_0$ and $E_0$. Thus $k_BT=E_0/\beta$ and physical volume is $\ell_0^d$ times numerical volume. Clause 8 is a separate formal dimensionless continuation with $\beta=0$ and fixed $z>0$ treated as a mathematical input; it lies outside the positive-temperature physical premises and has no SI temperature or pressure interpretation. Each clause is a separate conditional conclusion; no hypothesis of a stronger clause is implicit in a weaker one.

1. **Stable power-tempered free cubes.** Under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, for a stable power-tempered pair potential $\phi$ with the exact constants and tail bound of [[def-tdmath-stable-power-tempered-particle-model]], the free-cube standard positional grand partition sums $\Xi_L(z,\beta)$ have a finite reduced-pressure limit
$$p(z,\beta)=\lim_{L\to\infty}L^{-d}\log\Xi_L(z,\beta).$$

2. **Stable regular interior canonical rates and duality.** Under full $\mathrm{AC}$, for a stable regular potential with the decreasing integrable tail of [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]], the free-cube exact-$N$ rate $F_\beta(\rho)$ exists for every interior attainable density $\rho>0$ and every sequence $N_L/L^d\to\rho$. The free grand reduced pressure
$$P(\alpha,\beta)=\lim_{L\to\infty}L^{-d}\log\Xi_L(e^\alpha,\beta)$$
satisfies
$$P(\alpha,\beta)=\sup_{\rho\geq0}\{F_\beta(\rho)+\alpha\rho\},\qquad F_\beta(\rho)=\inf_{\alpha\in\mathbb R}\{P(\alpha,\beta)-\alpha\rho\}$$
on the closed effective domain of $F_\beta$. This does not assert an exact-$N$ limit at an excluded endpoint.

3. **Superstable regular grand variation.** Under $\mathrm{AC}$, the ultrafilter extension principle, $\mathrm{DC}$, and $\mathrm{HB}$, for a superstable regular potential and $z,\beta>0$, the normalized unit-Poisson partition rate exists for both free and periodic cubes:
$$p_Q(z,\beta)=\lim_{L\to\infty}L^{-d}\log E_{Q_{\Lambda_L}}\!\left[z^{N_{\Lambda_L}}e^{-\beta H_{L,b}}\right] =-\min_{P\in\mathcal P^1_{\rm stat}}\{I(P)+\beta\Phi(P)-\rho(P)\log z\},\quad b\in\{\mathrm{free},\mathrm{per}\}.$$
Here $Q_{\Lambda_L}$ is unit-intensity Poisson, $\mathcal P^1_{\rm stat}$ is the stationary finite-intensity law space, $I$ is specific relative entropy to $Q$, $\rho$ is intensity, and $\Phi$ is positional energy density, all as defined in [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]]. The minimizer set is nonempty and compact in the local-tame topology $\tau_L$ of [[def-tdmath-local-tame-topology]]. The standard $1/N!$ Lebesgue positional partition has reduced pressure $p_Q+1$; in $d=3$ its physical pressure is $E_0(p_Q+1)/(\beta\ell_0^3)$ Pa.

4. **Arbitrary free-wall shapes and fixed-particle limits.** Under full $\mathrm{AC}$, for the same superstable regular interaction, the free-wall grand reduced pressure along every van Hove sequence, as defined in [[def-tdmath-van-hove-sequence]], tends to the free-cube reduced pressure. At every interior attainable $\rho>0$, the free-wall exact-$N_k$ positional rate along every van Hove sequence with $N_k/|\Omega_k|\to\rho$ tends to $F_\beta(\rho)$. No stability-only arbitrary-shape upper bound or excluded-endpoint conclusion is asserted.

5. **Periodic and free local positional equivalence.** For the same superstable regular interaction and positive $\beta$ as in clause 3, under the four choice assumptions in that clause, if $\rho>0$ is interior attainable, $N_L/L^d\to\rho$, and $z>0$ is a finite supporting activity, the periodic exact-$N_L$ rate is $F_\beta(\rho)$ and its periodized empirical field concentrates in every open $\tau_L$ neighborhood of the grand variational minimizer set. The free exact-$N_L$ empirical field has the same neighborhood concentration. Here the periodized empirical field $R_{L,\omega}$ is the spatial average of translations of the periodic continuation, as defined in [[def-tdmath-periodized-empirical-field]], and convergence uses the outer-probability convention explicitly defined in [[lem-tdmath-canonical-empirical-field-conditioning]]. These statements concern spatially averaged local-tame observables, not the raw finite-box law at a fixed origin.

6. **A selected shrinking positional energy window.** Under clause 5, if $\beta\mapsto F_\beta(\rho)$ is differentiable at $\beta>0$ and the supporting grand variational minimizer is a singleton $P_*$, there exists a specific sequence $\delta_L\downarrow0$ for which the periodic exact-$N_L$ positional shell
$$\left|H_{L,\mathrm{per}}/L^d+\partial_\beta F_\beta(\rho)\right|\leq\delta_L$$
is eventually defined and its periodized empirical field converges in probability in $\tau_L$ to $P_*$. The free and periodic exact-$N_L$ laws and the matching periodic grand law have the same limiting empirical field. The width is selected by the proof; no arbitrary shell width or zero-width energy surface is covered.

7. **Uniform tempered exterior boundary.** Under full $\mathrm{AC}$, a superstable regular interaction, a genuine finite-valued positive core with divergent radial integral as in [[lem-tdmath-superquadratic-positive-core]], and fixed $z,\beta>0$, the free-wall grand pressure converges uniformly over the exact square-count exterior class $\Omega(t)$ defined in [[thm-tdmath-uniform-tempered-exterior-pressure]], for each finite $t$. Its limit is the free-cube pressure. This class excludes volume-filling external fields.

8. **Retained hard-exclusion zero-parameter branch.** Let $d\geq1$ and let $\phi$ be superstable and regular in the exact sense of [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]]. In the separate formal continuation with fixed dimensionless activity $z>0$ and $\beta=0$, under $\mathrm{AC}$, the ultrafilter extension principle, $\mathrm{DC}$, and $\mathrm{HB}$, the model that retains the hard-forbidden set $B=\{x:\phi(x)=+\infty\}$ has the free and periodic rates and minimizers specified in [[thm-tdmath-retained-hard-zero-beta-limit]]. This is outside the positive-temperature physical premises. It is the activity-weighted model with forbidden pairs still excluded, not the unrestricted Poisson model unless $|B|=0$.

All clauses are conditional model deductions. None says that the adopted postulate describes a particular material. The variational minimizers above are not thereby identified as DLR laws.

row.title: Conditional entropy chain and disjoint-block bounds

items.title: Conditional entropy chain and disjoint-block bounds
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $X_1,\ldots,X_m$ be standard-Borel spaces, let $Q_i$ be probability measures on $X_i$, and let $P$ be a probability on $\prod_{i=1}^mX_i$. Write $P_i$ for its $i$th marginal and use the directional extended relative entropy $D(\cdot\Vert\cdot)$ of [[def-tdmath-finite-region-relative-entropy]]. Then
$$D(P\Vert Q_1\otimes\cdots\otimes Q_m)\geq\sum_{i=1}^mD(P_i\Vert Q_i).$$
If the left side is finite, the conditional chain rule gives the stronger equality
$$D(P\Vert\textstyle\bigotimes_iQ_i)=D(P_1\Vert Q_1)+\sum_{i=2}^m E_P\,D(P_{X_i\mid X_1,\ldots,X_{i-1}}\Vert Q_i),$$
and each conditional increment is at least $D(P_i\Vert Q_i)$. If the left side is infinite, the displayed inequality is understood in the extended order and is automatic. This applies to finitely many disjoint spatial blocks after their particle counts and positions have been fixed; zero-occupancy blocks contribute zero.

items.title: Measurable information contraction and Pinsker bound
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $P,Q$ be probability measures on a measurable space and let $T$ be a measurable map to another measurable space. Then
$$D(T_*P\Vert T_*Q)\leq D(P\Vert Q),\qquad \|P-Q\|_{\rm TV}:=\sup_A|P(A)-Q(A)|\leq\sqrt{D(P\Vert Q)/2}.$$
The entropy convention is the directional KL definition of [[def-kullback-leibler-divergence]], and the total-variation convention is the event-supremum convention of [[def-total-variation-distance-for-probability-laws]]. The inequality remains valid when $D=+\infty$.

items.title: Interacting marked phase-space and reference measures
items.statement:
Assume AC. Fix $d\geq1$ and let $\phi:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}$ be the numerical even Borel pair potential. Assume the stability, cell-superstability, lower-regularity, and decreasing-integrable-tail conditions of [[def-csm-stable-superstable-continuum-interaction]], with its fixed cell side $\ell$, and the superstable regular interaction, unit-coordinate, and periodic-image conventions of [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]]. These are model hypotheses; the definitions do not prove that a particular material satisfies them. Use the finite-region phase-space and statistical-state conventions of [[def-csm-statistical-state-observable]].

Let $E_0>0$ joules be the energy unit, $\ell_0>0$ metres the length unit, $m>0$ kilograms the particle mass, and $p_*>0$ kg m s$^{-1}$ the momentum reference. Positions $x=q/\ell_0$ are dimensionless numerical coordinates; write $V_L=L^d$ for numerical volume. The dimensionless positional energy $U_{L,bc}$ is the physical pair energy divided by $E_0$, with $bc\in\{\mathrm{free},\mathrm{per}\}$ and the exact image convention above. If $T>0$ kelvin, put $\beta_{\rm phys}=1/(k_BT)$ in J$^{-1}$ and $b=\beta_{\rm phys}E_0=E_0/(k_BT)>0$.

Let $Q_L$ be the unit-intensity Poisson probability on positional configurations in $\Lambda_L=[0,L)^d$, defined by [[def-tdmath-poisson-configuration-reference]]. Its $N$-particle conditional law $Q_{L,N}$ is uniform on the unordered simple $N$-point configurations; in labelled coordinates it is $L^{-dN}dx_1\cdots dx_N$ on the no-collision set. On an $N$-point configuration, attach one momentum $p_x\in\mathbb R^d$ to each point and use the symmetric product reference $r^{\otimes q}$ with $r(dp)=dp/p_*^d$. The finite phase reference is
$$R_{L,N}(dq,dp):=Q_L(dq)\,r^{\otimes q}(dp)\,1_{\{N(q)=N\}}.$$
It is sigma-finite; the factor $e^{-V_L}/N!$ from the Poisson sector is retained. In physical coordinates the corresponding one-particle product scale is $h_{\rm ref}^d=\ell_0^dp_*^d$, an action to the power $d$; it is a reference convention, not a derived quantum constant.

For a marked configuration define the total dimensionless energy
$$\mathcal H_{L,bc}(q,p)=U_{L,bc}(q)+\sum_{x\in q}K(p_x),\qquad K(p)=\frac{|p|^2}{2mE_0}.$$
For $b>0$, [[lem-csm-gaussian-mark-moments]] gives $\kappa_b=\int e^{-bK}r(dp)=(2\pi mE_0/(bp_*^2))^{d/2}$ and the probability kernel $\nu_b(dp)=\kappa_b^{-1}e^{-bK(p)}r(dp)$. Whenever the positional canonical partition is finite and positive, nonnegative product integration [[thm-tonelli-theorem-for-sigma-finite-product-spaces]] gives exact identities
$$Z^{\rm ph}_{Q,L,N,bc}(b)=\int e^{-b\mathcal H_{L,bc}}dR_{L,N}=\kappa_b^N Z^{\rm pos}_{Q,L,N,bc}(b),\qquad C^{\rm ph}_{L,N,bc}=C^{\rm pos}_{L,N,bc}\,\nu_b^{\otimes q}.$$
Here $Z^{\rm pos}_{Q,L,N,bc}=E_{Q_L}[1_{\{N(q)=N\}}e^{-bU_{L,bc}}]$ and the canonical probabilities are the normalized respective integrands. Under a full grand preparation of activity $z_{\rm ph}$, integrating each momentum changes the positional activity to $z=z_{\rm ph}\kappa_b$; thus a positional activity $z=e^\alpha$ corresponds to $z_{\rm ph}=e^\alpha/\kappa_b$. These are exact definitions and normalizations; they do not assert dynamical equilibration or finite-volume grand convergence. For periodic boundary conditions, simultaneous translation of all positions modulo the period preserves $R_{L,N}$ and $\mathcal H_{L,\mathrm{per}}$: the conditional position law is uniform on the torus, the mark reference is invariant under relabelling points, and the image energy depends only on pair displacements. Hence normalized canonical and finite band restrictions are torus-translation invariant.

items.title: Marked periodic continuation and local restriction
items.design_state: draft-authoring
items.statement:
Let $\Omega$ be the positional configuration space of [[def-tdmath-poisson-configuration-reference]]. The **marked configuration space** $\Omega^{\rm mark}$ consists of marked point sets $\xi\subseteq\mathbb R^d\times\mathbb R^d$ with spatial projection $q=\{x\in\mathbb R^d:\exists p\in\mathbb R^d,\ (x,p)\in\xi\}$ that is simple and locally finite, and with exactly one mark $p_x$ paired to each $x\in q$. Its sigma-algebra is generated by the marked counts $N_{A\times C}(\xi)=\#\{(x,p)\in\xi:x\in A,\ p\in C\}$ for bounded Borel $A\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ and Borel $C\subseteq\mathbb R^d$. The positional projection is $\pi(\xi)=q\in\Omega$. For a bounded Borel set $\Delta$, the **marked local restriction** is $\xi_\Delta=\{(x,p)\in\xi:x\in\Delta\}$ with the induced count sigma-algebra; write $N_\Delta(\xi)=\#\xi_\Delta$. A **marked-local observable on $\Delta$** is a real measurable function of $\xi_\Delta$; it is bounded when its supremum norm is finite.

Let $d\geq1$, $L>0$, and $\Lambda_L=[0,L)^d$. A finite marked configuration consists of a finite simple set of positions $q\subseteq\Lambda_L$ and a mark map $p:q\to\mathbb R^d$, as in [[def-csm-full-marked-model]]. Its **marked periodic continuation** is
$$\omega^{\mathrm{per}}_{L,q,p}:=\{(x+Lk,p_x):x\in q,\ k\in\mathbb Z^d\}.$$
The spatial positions in this set are distinct: if $x+Lk=y+Lj$ for $x,y\in[0,L)^d$, then coordinatewise $x-y=L(j-k)$ forces $j=k$ and $x=y$. Every bounded spatial region meets finitely many lattice translates of the finite set $q$, so the continuation has a locally finite spatial projection.

For a bounded Borel set $\Delta\subseteq\mathbb R^d$, define its **marked local restriction** by
$$\omega^{\mathrm{per}}_{L,q,p}|_\Delta:=\{(y,p_x)\in\omega^{\mathrm{per}}_{L,q,p}:y\in\Delta\}.$$
This is an element of $\Omega^{\rm mark}$, with the induced sigma-algebra of marked counts above. If $\Delta\subseteq\Lambda_L$, the restriction is exactly the original marked points with positions in $\Delta$.

references.title: H.-O. Georgii and H. Zessin, Large deviations and the maximum entropy principle for marked point random fields
references.locator: Section 2.2, periodic continuation and marked empirical fields; the finite marked restriction is defined explicitly here.

items.title: Existence of the independent Gaussian-marked positional lift
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $P$ be any probability law on the simple locally finite positional configuration space $\Omega$ of [[def-tdmath-poisson-configuration-reference]], and let $
u$ be a probability on the momentum mark space $\mathbb R^d$. Use the marked configuration space $\Omega^{m mark}$ and local restrictions $\xi_\Delta$ of [[def-csm-marked-periodic-continuation]]. Define translations by $T_yq=\{x+y:x\in q\}$ and $T_y^{m mark}\xi=\{(x+y,p):(x,p)\in\xi\}$. Then there is a unique probability law $P^{m mark}$ on $\Omega^{m mark}$ whose positional projection is $P$ and whose marks, conditional on the entire positional configuration, are independent with common law $
u$. If $P$ is translation invariant, meaning $(T_y)_\#P=P$ for every $y\in\mathbb R^d$, then $(T_y^{m mark})_\#P^{m mark}=P^{m mark}$ for every $y$. For the Gaussian $
u_b$ of [[def-csm-full-marked-model]], this is the independent Gaussian-marked positional lift. This is a mathematical marking construction, not a physical preparation or a convergence result.

items.title: Total-energy concentration and controlled canonical windows
items.statement:
Assume AC, the ultrafilter extension principle, DC, and HB. Use the model and dimensionless energy $\mathcal H_{L,\mathrm{per}}$ of [[def-csm-full-marked-model]]. Let $L_n\to\infty$, $V_n=L_n^d$, and integers $N_n$ satisfy $N_n/V_n\to\rho>0$, where $\rho$ is an interior attainable density for the positional canonical rate. Fix $b>0$. Assume $F_b(\rho)$ is the periodic exact-particle log-partition rate supplied by [[thm-tdmath-periodic-fixed-n-limit]] for every $b'$ in a neighborhood of $b$, and is differentiable at $b$. Write $C_n^{\rm ph}$ for the full fixed-$N_n$ canonical law, and define
$$e_b(\rho)=-\partial_bF_b(\rho)+\frac{d\rho}{2b}.$$
Then, for each fixed $\varepsilon>0$, there exist $c_\varepsilon>0$ and $n_0$ such that
$$C_n^{\rm ph}\!\left(\left|\mathcal H_{L_n,\mathrm{per}}/V_n-e_b(\rho)\right|>\varepsilon\right)\le 2e^{-c_\varepsilon V_n}\quad(n\ge n_0).$$
Consequently there is a nonincreasing sequence $\delta_n\downarrow0$ for which the full phase band
$$A_n=\{N=N_n,\ |\mathcal H_{L_n,\mathrm{per}}/V_n-e_b(\rho)|\le\delta_n\}$$
has $C_n^{\rm ph}(A_n)\to1$. It has positive finite phase-reference measure for all sufficiently large $n$. This constructs a controlled shrinking window; it makes no claim about every prescribed shell width or an exact energy surface.

items.title: Classical full-phase interacting ensemble preparations
items.statement:
Fix the model, physical reference conventions, mass, potential and energy window specified by [[def-csm-full-marked-model]] and [[thm-csm-total-canonical-window]]. Identify the action reference a_0 of [[post-csm-counting-and-physical-observables]] with h_ref=ℓ_0p_* from the marked model. Adopt the following alternative preparations whenever their normalizations are finite and positive:

1. At fixed exact particle number $N$, controls and $T>0$, use the canonical density proportional to $e^{-\beta H}$ relative to the declared phase reference, as in [[post-csm-canonical-preparation]].
2. For a sequence satisfying all hypotheses of [[thm-csm-total-canonical-window]]—including AC, the ultrafilter extension principle, DC, HB, an interior attainable density, the periodic exact-particle log-rate hypothesis near $b$, and differentiability at $b$—at fixed exact $N_n$ use the uniform full-phase reference law restricted to its constructed band $A_n$. “Uniform” means normalized restriction of that finite reference measure; it is an energy-window preparation, not a zero-width surface measure. This postulate makes no existence claim for that specific band when those theorem hypotheses fail.
3. For particle exchange, use the countable-sector grand preparation of [[post-csm-grand-preparation]]. Its full dimensionless activity is the fugacity $z_{\rm ph}:=e^{\beta_{\rm phys}\mu}>0$, where $\beta_{\rm phys}=1/(k_BT)$ in J$^{-1}$ and the chemical potential $\mu$ is in J per particle. When matching positional activity $z=e^\alpha$ at inverse temperature $b$, choose $z_{\rm ph}=z/\kappa_b$, as in [[def-csm-full-marked-model]].

These laws are adopted statistical preparations. They do not follow from Hamiltonian energy conservation, do not assert that any isolated dynamics reaches these distributions, and do not encode an experimental observation. The band sequence is the particular controlled shrinking window constructed conditionally by [[thm-csm-total-canonical-window]].

items.statement: Assume AC and the hypotheses and notation of [[thm-csm-total-canonical-window]]. Let $R_n=R_{L_n,N_n}$ be the finite phase reference of [[def-csm-full-marked-model]], let $A_n$ be the constructed band, and set $M_n^{\rm ph}(E)=R_n(E\cap A_n)/R_n(A_n)$. Let $C_n^{\rm ph}$ be the full fixed-$N_n$ canonical probability. Then $D_n=D(M_n^{\rm ph}\Vert C_n^{\rm ph})$ satisfies $D_n/V_n\to0$. This is a mathematical statement about a normalized measure restriction; it does not assert $D_n\to0$ or global total-variation convergence.

items.title: Full phase shell marginal satisfies the positional variational bound
items.statement:
Assume AC, the ultrafilter extension principle, DC and HB, the exact superstable regular pair interaction and periodic-image convention of [[def-csm-full-marked-model]], and integer side lengths $L_n\to\infty$ with exact particle numbers $N_n/V_n\to\rho>0$ at an interior attainable density. Fix $b>0$. Assume the positional canonical log rate is $F_b(\rho)$, and choose finite $\alpha$ with
$$P_{\rm Leb}(α,b)=F_b(ρ)+αρ,$$
where $P_{\rm Leb}$ is the grand pressure per numerical volume with Lebesgue $1/N!$ normalization. Let the positional grand variational minimizer of [[thm-tdmath-continuum-variational-pressure]] at activity $\exp(\alpha)$ and inverse temperature $b$ be the singleton $\{P_*\}$. Let $R_n=R_{L_n,N_n}$ be the phase reference of [[def-csm-full-marked-model]], let $A_n$ be the band of [[thm-csm-total-canonical-window]], set $M_n^{\rm ph}(E)=R_n(E\cap A_n)/R_n(A_n)$, and let $B_n$ be its positional marginal. For any local-tame test $f$, write $B_n[f]=E_{B_n}f(\omega^{(L_n)})$ and $C_n^{\rm pos}[f]=E_{C_n^{\rm pos}}f(\omega^{(L_n)})$, where $\omega^{(L_n)}$ is the periodic continuation. Let $\bar B_n$ be the barycenter of $R_{L_n,\omega}$ under $B_n$. Then $\bar B_n$ converges to $P_*$ in $\tau_L$, equivalently $B_n[f]\to P_*(f)$ for every local-tame $f$; also $C_n^{\rm pos}[f]\to P_*(f)$ for every such $f$. The periodized empirical fields of the exact-$N_n$ canonical laws converge in probability in $\tau_L$ to $P_*$ by [[thm-tdmath-periodic-fixed-n-limit]], and $P_*$ has intensity $\rho$. Here $P_*$ is an infinite-volume positional variational state; no finite-volume grand-canonical local convergence or DLR identification is asserted.

items.title: Spatial random-occupation conditional mark entropy bound
items.statement:
Assume AC and the hypotheses of [[thm-csm-full-shell-positional-minimizer]]. Let $M_n^{\rm ph}$ be the normalized phase-reference restriction to $A_n$, and let $B_n$ be its positional marginal. Given the full position configuration $q$, let $b_{n,A}(\cdot|q)$ be the shell conditional law of marks on the marked local restriction of [[def-csm-marked-periodic-continuation]]. By torus translation invariance, represent any bounded Borel region $\Delta$ by a fixed translate inside $\Lambda_{L_n}$ for all sufficiently large $n$. Choose an axis-parallel half-open cube $C\supseteq\Delta$ of side $\ell>0$, independent of $n$, and pack $L_n^{\rm pack}=\lfloor L_n/\ell\rfloor^d$ disjoint translates of $C$ into the periodic cube, so $L_n^{\rm pack}/V_n\to1/|C|$. For the independent Gaussian mark reference $\nu_b$ of [[def-csm-full-marked-model]],
$$E_{B_n}D(b_{n,\Delta}(\cdot|q)||\nu_b^{\otimes N_\Delta(q)})\leq D(M_n^{\rm ph}||C_n^{\rm ph})/L_n^{\rm pack}.$$
Thus the left side tends to zero. When $\Delta$ itself is an axis-parallel half-open cube, take $C=\Delta$ to obtain the stated packing rate $1/|\Delta|$. Occupancy $N_\Delta(q)$ is random; the comparison is for the full spatially selected set of particles, not a fixed set of labels.

items.title: Full interacting shell, canonical, and variational-grand local marked equivalence
items.statement:
Assume AC and the hypotheses and notation of [[thm-csm-full-shell-positional-minimizer]], including its AC, ultrafilter extension principle, DC, and HB assumptions. Fix a bounded Borel region $\Delta$ and use the marked periodic continuation and local restriction defined in [[def-csm-marked-periodic-continuation]]. By translating $\Delta$ and the spatial argument of $G$ together, take a representative with $\Delta\subseteq[0,\infty)^d$; then $\Delta\subseteq\Lambda_{L_n}$ for all sufficiently large $n$. This translation preserves the expectations because the finite laws are torus-translation invariant and the limiting independent mark lift of the stationary positional state is stationary. Let $M_n^{\rm ph}$ be the uniform full-phase band law, $C_n^{\rm ph}$ the exact-$N_n$ full canonical law, and $P_*$ the singleton positional grand variational minimizer. Give points of $P_*$ independent marks with kernel $\nu_b$ of [[def-csm-full-marked-model]], and denote the resulting infinite marked law by $P_*^{\rm mark}$, whose existence is supplied by [[lem-csm-gaussian-marked-lift-existence]]. For finite-volume expectations, evaluate $G$ on the restriction $\omega^{\rm per}_{L_n,q,p}|_\Delta$; under $P_*^{\rm mark}$, evaluate it on $\xi_\Delta$. Then for every bounded marked-local observable $G$ on $\Delta$ in the sense of [[def-csm-marked-periodic-continuation]],
$$E_{M_n^{ph}}G\to E_{P_*^{mark}}G,\qquad E_{C_n^{ph}}G\to E_{P_*^{mark}}G.$$
The matched full grand activity is $\exp(\alpha)/\kappa_b$ by the normalization identity in [[def-csm-full-marked-model]]; $P_*^{\rm mark}$ is the independent-Gaussian marked lift associated with that positional variational minimizer. If additionally $|G|\leq C(1+N_\Delta)$, shell convergence also holds for $G$. This is fixed-region convergence, not uniform over growing regions or arbitrary unbounded momentum observables. No finite-volume grand-canonical convergence or DLR converse is asserted.

items.title: Local kinetic energy and first and second momentum expectations
items.statement:
Assume AC and the hypotheses of [[thm-csm-local-mark-kl-bound]]. Fix a bounded half-open cube $\Delta\subseteq[0,\infty)^d$; then $\Delta\subseteq\Lambda_{L_n}$ for all sufficiently large $n$. By torus translation invariance this placement gives the same limits as any fixed translate of the cube. Let $N_\Delta(q)=\#(q\cap\Delta)$. For $b>0$ and $K(p)=|p|^2/(2mE_0)$, the full shell law satisfies
$$E_{M_n^{ph}}\sum_{x\in q\cap\Delta}K(p_x)\to dρ|Δ|/(2b),\quad E_{M_n^{ph}}\sum_{x\in q\cap\Delta}p_{x,i}\to0,$$
$$E_{M_n^{ph}}\sum_{x\in q\cap\Delta}p_{x,i}p_{x,j}\to(mE_0ρ|Δ|/b)\delta_{ij}.$$
The corresponding canonical and marked variational-grand laws have the same limits by their independent Gaussian marking. Momentum is in kg m s^-1, E_0K is in joules, and b=E_0/(k_BT) is dimensionless. These conclusions concern only the named moments, not every unbounded mark observable.

Use $\|P-Q\|_{\rm TV}=\sup_A|P(A)-Q(A)|$. This is a finite-model claim, not an experimental assertion.

The refuted implication is: for every sequence of laws $Q_N\ll P_N$, if $N^{-1}D(Q_N\Vert P_N)\to0$, $H_N/N\to\epsilon\theta$ in $Q_N$-probability, and $N^{-1}H_{\rm Sh}(Q_N)\to h(\theta)$, then the first-coordinate marginal of $Q_N$ converges in event-supremum total variation to Bernoulli$(\theta)$. items.title: A volume-preserving diffeomorphism preserves its induced Borel measure
items.statement:
Assume countable choice. Let $M$ be a Hausdorff second-countable smooth
$n$-manifold and let $\eta$ be a positive smooth density, with Borel
coefficients as in [[def-borel-measurable-nonnegative-density-on-a-manifold]].
Let $\mu_\eta$ be the intrinsic chart-gluing Borel measure of
[[thm-density-measure-is-independent-of-the-chart-gluing]]. If
$\phi:M\to M$ is a $C^1$
diffeomorphism satisfying $\phi^*\eta=\eta$, then
$$\mu_\eta(\phi^{-1}(E))=\mu_\eta(E)$$
for every Borel set $E\subseteq M$. The total measure may be infinite.

references.title: Gerald B. Folland, Real Analysis, 2nd ed., §11.4 and Theorem 2.47

items.title: Hamiltonian phase, complete-domain flow and reference measure
items.statement:
Adopt $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the density-measure construction
([[def-countable-choice]]). A **Hamiltonian phase datum** consists of a
Hausdorff second-countable smooth manifold $M$ of finite even dimension $2n$
without boundary, a symplectic form $\omega$ on $M$, and an autonomous smooth
function $H:M\to\mathbb R$. Here symplectic means that $\omega$ is a smooth
closed two-form and is nondegenerate at every point
([[def-symplectic-form-and-symplectic-manifold]]). The Hamiltonian vector field
$X_H$ is the unique smooth field satisfying $\iota_{X_H}\omega=dH$
([[def-hamiltonian-vector-field-and-hamiltonian-function]],
[[thm-hamiltonian-vector-fields-exist-uniquely-for-smooth-functions]]).
For each $z\in M$, let $I_z\subseteq\mathbb R$ be the maximal open interval
containing $0$ on which the unique maximal $C^\infty$ integral curve
$\gamma_z:I_z\to M$ satisfying $\dot\gamma_z(t)=X_H(\gamma_z(t))$ and
$\gamma_z(0)=z$ is defined; its existence and uniqueness follow from the
smooth ODE theorem ([[thm-fundamental-theorem-for-autonomous-smooth-odes]]).
Set $D=\{(t,z):z\in M,\ t\in I_z\}$ and define the maximal local flow
$\Phi:D\to M$ by $\Phi(t,z)=\gamma_z(t)$. Write $\Phi_t(z)=\Phi(t,z)$ when
$(t,z)\in D$. Uniqueness gives $\Phi_0(z)=z$ and
$\Phi_t(\Phi_s(z))=\Phi_{t+s}(z)$ whenever the terms are defined.
The domain $D$ is open, and in local charts $\Phi$ is smooth in the initial
state and $C^1$ in time, as supplied by the stated ODE theorem.
Completeness of the flow on all of $M$ is not part of this datum.

A Borel set $R\subseteq M$ is a **complete invariant domain** for this datum
if $\{t\}\times R\subseteq D$ and $\Phi_t(R)=R$ for every
$t\in\mathbb R$. Thus each restricted map $\Phi_t|_R:R\to R$ is defined
everywhere on $R$. The definition makes no assertion that $M$ itself is
complete or that such an $R$ has finite measure.

The symplectic orientation has volume form $\Omega=\omega^n/n!$
([[cor-symplectic-manifolds-have-a-canonical-orientation-and-volume-form]]).
For a fixed positive reference action $a_0$, define the positive smooth density
$\eta_0=|\Omega|/a_0^n$ and let $m_0$ be its intrinsic Borel measure
([[def-density-bundle-and-smooth-density]],
[[def-borel-measurable-nonnegative-density-on-a-manifold]],
[[thm-density-measure-is-independent-of-the-chart-gluing]],
[[thm-a-positive-smooth-density-defines-a-locally-finite-radon-measure]]).
The measure $m_0$ may have infinite total mass. Use SI units for a physical
interpretation. In a standard mechanical cotangent chart, $q^i$ has unit m,
$p_i$ has unit kg m/s, $H$ has unit J, $\omega$ and $a_0$ have unit J s, and
$\eta_0$ is dimensionless. The scale $a_0$ is a normalization convention and
does not assert quantization.

An **ensemble** on $R$ is a Borel probability measure $\mu$ on $R$, distinct
from an individual trajectory. If $\mu$ has density $\rho$ with respect to
$m_0|_R$, then $\rho\ge0$ is Borel and $\int_R\rho\,dm_0=1$. For $\beta>0$,
the **canonical probability**, when it exists, is the Borel measure
$$\mu_\beta(B)=Z_\beta^{-1}\int_B e^{-\beta H}\,dm_0,\qquad Z_\beta=\int_R e^{-\beta H}\,dm_0,$$
for Borel $B\subseteq R$, provided $0<Z_\beta<\infty$. For a
temperature-parameterized physical interpretation, take $T>0$ as an absolute
temperature in K and $k_B>0$ as a supplied energy-temperature conversion
constant in J/K, and set $\beta=(k_BT)^{-1}$ in J$^{-1}$.

Daniel Arovas, Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, §3.2
David Tong, Statistical Physics, §§1.2.1 and 1.3.1

items.title: Green–Kubo covariance limit under absolute integrability
items.statement:
Let $(\Xi,\mathcal F,\mathbb P)$ be a probability space and let
$V:\mathbb R\times\Xi\to\mathbb R^d$ be jointly measurable for the completed
product of Lebesgue measure and $\mathbb P$. Assume $\mathbb E[V(t)]=0$ for
every $t$, $\mathbb E|V(0)|^2<\infty$, and second-order stationarity in the
explicit sense that each covariance below is finite and
$$C_{ij}(s):=\mathbb E[V_i(u)V_j(u+s)]$$
is independent of $u\in\mathbb R$ for every $s\in\mathbb R$ and every
$1\le i,j\le d$. For $T>0$, the Lebesgue integral
$X(T)=\int_0^T V(s)\,ds$ exists almost surely and in $L^2$. Define
$$\operatorname{Cov}(X(T))_{ij} =\mathbb E[(X_i(T)-\mathbb EX_i(T))(X_j(T)-\mathbb EX_j(T))];$$
the centered hypothesis makes these means zero. Then
$$\operatorname{Cov}(X_i(T),X_j(T)) =\int_0^T(T-s)\big(C_{ij}(s)+C_{ji}(s)\big)\,ds.$$
If each $C_{ij}$ is absolutely integrable on $[0,\infty)$, then
$$\frac{\operatorname{Cov}(X(T))}{2T}\longrightarrow D,\qquad D_{ij}=\frac12\int_0^\infty\big(C_{ij}(s)+C_{ji}(s)\big)\,ds,$$
and $D$ is positive semidefinite. This is a variance-growth conclusion; it
does not assert a central limit theorem or identify a transport coefficient.

references.title: MIT OpenCourseWare, 22.103 Microscopic Theory of Transport, Lecture 3, pp. 1–4
David Tong, Classical Dynamics, complete author-hosted lecture notes, §4.2

items.title: Ergodicity and mixing for a selected probability map
items.statement:
Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu,T)$ be a probability-preserving system: $\mu(X)=1$,
$T:X\to X$ is measurable, and $\mu(T^{-1}E)=\mu(E)$ for every
$E\in\mathcal A$
([[def-measure-preserving-transformation-and-system]]). The **ergodicity**
convention is that every strictly invariant set $E\in\mathcal A$, meaning
$T^{-1}E=E$, has measure zero or one, as in
[[def-ergodic-measure-preserving-system]].

For $E,F\in\mathcal A$ and integer $n\ge0$, put
$$d_n(E,F)=\mu(E\cap T^{-n}F)-\mu(E)\mu(F).$$
The map is **strongly mixing** if $d_n(E,F)\to0$ for every measurable pair
$(E,F)$. It is **weakly mixing** if
$$\frac1N\sum_{n=0}^{N-1}|d_n(E,F)|\longrightarrow0$$
for every such pair as $N\to\infty$. Thus the absolute value is inside the
Cesàro average, exactly as in [[def-strong-and-weak-mixing]]. These are
properties of the selected discrete map $T$ and its selected invariant
probability $\mu$; no flow-level property is implicit.

references.title: Peter Sarig, Lecture Notes on Ergodic Theory, Definition 1.4
E. H. El Abdalaoui and F. Vivaldi, Ergodic Theory and Dynamical Systems, Definitions 2.32 and 2.35

items.title: Adopted classical Hamiltonian dynamics and preparation
items.statement:
For a selected finite-dimensional nonrelativistic classical model, adopt a
Hamiltonian phase datum [[def-csm-dk-hamiltonian-flow-measure]] and interpret
each point of its manifold $M$ as a complete instantaneous model state. The
Hamiltonian $H:M\to\mathbb R$ is the model's supplied primitive energy
function; no derivation from a Lagrangian is assumed here. Choose a complete
invariant domain $R$ and a prepared Borel probability measure $\mu_0$ on $R$.
For each initial state $z_0\in R$, the unforced state curve is the smooth map
$z_{z_0}:\mathbb R\to M$ defined by $z_{z_0}(t)=\Phi_t(z_0)$ using the flow
from the phase datum; complete invariance ensures $z_{z_0}(t)\in R$ for every
$t$. The preparation is a probability law over possible
phase points; it is not an individual trajectory or a claim that an ensemble
was experimentally sampled.

Use SI units for the physical interpretation. In a standard canonical
cotangent chart, $q^i$ are generalized position coordinates in m and $p_i$
are their canonical conjugate momenta in kg m/s; identifying $p_i$ with
mechanical momentum requires that additional model convention. The Hamiltonian
has units J and time has units s. The reference action $a_0$ in the
mathematical definition has units J s and is a normalization convention.
If a canonical-temperature model is additionally selected, take $T>0$ as
absolute temperature in K and adopt $k_B>0$ as a primitive
energy-temperature conversion constant of this formulation, with units J/K.
Set $\beta=(k_BT)^{-1}$ in J$^{-1}$ and use the associated weight only when
its partition integral is finite and positive. This postulate does not assert
that the canonical law is normalizable for every Hamiltonian or that these
adopted parameters describe nature.

references.title: David Tong, Classical Dynamics, complete author-hosted lecture notes, §4.2
Daniel Arovas, Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, §3.2
David Tong, Statistical Physics, §§1.2.1 and 1.3.1
David Tong, Statistical Physics, §2.1

items.physical_scope: A specified smooth nonrelativistic Hamiltonian and prepared probability law; no generic ergodicity, equilibration, thermostat identification, or claim about nature.

items.title: Exact finite-time response on a compact Hamiltonian phase
items.statement:
Let $(M,\omega,H,\Phi,m_0)$ be a nonempty compact symplectic phase datum
without boundary, with $H\in C^\infty(M,\mathbb R)$. Let
$A,B\in C^\infty(M,\mathbb R)$ be observables, let $\beta>0$, and assume
$Z_\beta=\int_Me^{-\beta H}\,dm_0$ is finite and positive. Put
$d\mu_\beta=Z_\beta^{-1}e^{-\beta H}\,dm_0$. For $T>0$ and every
$t\in[0,T]$, choose
$h\in C^\infty([0,T],\mathbb R)$ and perturb the Hamiltonian to
$H_\epsilon(t,z)=H(z)-\epsilon h(t)B(z)$, where $\epsilon$ is dimensionless.
In SI, time has unit s. If $H$ is in J, $A$ has units $[A]$, and $B$ has
units $[B]$, then $h$ has units J$/[B]$, $\beta$ has units J$^{-1}$, and the
response derivative has units $[A]$.

Start every perturbed trajectory at the same unperturbed initial law
$\mu_\beta$ and define
$\langle A(t)\rangle_\epsilon=\int_M A(z_\epsilon(t;z))\,d\mu_\beta(z)$.
Then the derivative at $\epsilon=0$ exists and is
$$\left.\frac{d}{d\epsilon}\langle A(t)\rangle_\epsilon\right|_{\epsilon=0} =\int_0^t h(s)R_{AB}(t-s)\,ds,\qquad R_{AB}(u)=\beta\int_M(X_HB)(z)A(\Phi_u z)\,d\mu_\beta(z).$$
For constant $h(t)=h_0$, define the equilibrium correlation
$$C_{BA}(u)=\int_M(B-\langle B\rangle_\beta)(z) (A-\langle A\rangle_\beta)(\Phi_u z)\,d\mu_\beta(z).$$
Then the finite-time response is
$\beta h_0[C_{BA}(0)-C_{BA}(t)]$. If $C_{BA}(t)\to0$, its long-time limit
is $\beta h_0\operatorname{Cov}_{\mu_\beta}(B,A)$. No decay of this
correlation is assumed in the finite-time formula.

references.title: David Tong, Classical Dynamics, complete author-hosted lecture notes, §4.2
Daniel Arovas, Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, §3.2
MIT OpenCourseWare, 22.103 Microscopic Theory of Transport, Lecture 3, pp. 1–4

items.title: Hamiltonian recurrence under the exact finite-measure hypothesis
items.statement:
Let $(M,\omega,H,\Phi,m_0)$ be a Hamiltonian phase datum, let $R\subseteq M$
be a complete invariant Borel domain, and fix $\Delta>0$. Put
$T=\Phi_\Delta|_R$. Let $\mu$ be any finite Borel measure on $R$ invariant
under $T$. Then for every Borel $E\subseteq R$,
$\mu$-almost every $z\in E$ satisfies
$T^kz\in E$ for infinitely many integers $k\ge1$. The result is
almost-everywhere recurrence for this fixed sampled map; it is not a
pointwise statement about every initial state. The hypothesis also allows
finite invariant measures singular with respect to ambient Liouville volume.

references.title: David Tong, Classical Dynamics, complete author-hosted lecture notes, §4.2.3
Daniel Arovas, Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, §3.3

items.title: Invariant energy-weighted and regular-shell probabilities
items.statement:
Let $(M,\omega,H,\Phi,m_0)$ be a Hamiltonian phase datum and let $R$ be a
complete invariant Borel domain. If $w:\mathbb R\to[0,\infty]$ is Borel and
$$0<Z_w:=\int_R w(H)\,dm_0<\infty,$$
then
$\mu_w(B)=Z_w^{-1}\int_Bw(H)\,dm_0$ is an invariant Borel probability on
$R$. In particular, for $\beta>0$, the canonical density
$e^{-\beta H}/Z_\beta$ defines an invariant probability whenever
$Z_\beta=\int_R e^{-\beta H}\,dm_0$ is finite and positive.

There is also the following regular-shell conclusion. Assume full AC. Let
$O\subseteq\mathbb R^{2n}$ be open with canonical
$\omega=\sum_i dq^i\wedge dp_i$, let $H\in C^2(O,\mathbb R)$, and let
$J\subseteq\mathbb R$ be open. Suppose $\nabla H\ne0$ on $H^{-1}(J)$ and
$H^{-1}(K)$ is compact in $O$ for every compact $K\subset J$. For each
nonempty shell $\Sigma_E=H^{-1}(\{E\})$, the weighted area measure
$\mu_E$ of [[def-tdmath-regular-energy-shell]] satisfies
$0<\mu_E(1)<\infty$, and
$\widehat\mu_E=\mu_E/\mu_E(1)$ is invariant under every Hamiltonian flow
diffeomorphism preserving a full compact band containing $\Sigma_E$.
Critical levels and noncompact bands are outside this clause.

references.title: David Tong, Classical Dynamics, complete author-hosted lecture notes, §4.2.2
Daniel Arovas, Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, §3.2

items.title: Conditional sampled and continuous-time averages
items.statement:
Let $(M,\omega,H,\Phi,m_0)$ be a Hamiltonian phase datum and let $R$ be a
complete invariant Borel domain carrying a Borel probability $\mu$ such that
$\mu(\Phi_s^{-1}B)=\mu(B)$ for every $s\in\mathbb R$ and every Borel
$B\subseteq R$. Fix a sampling interval $\Delta>0$ and define the time map
$T=\Phi_\Delta|_R$. Assume this particular map is ergodic for $\mu$, meaning
that every Borel $E\subseteq R$ with $T^{-1}E=E$ has $\mu(E)\in\{0,1\}$.
For every real $f\in L^1(\mu)$, the sampled averages
$$\frac1N\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}f(T^jz)$$
converge $\mu$-almost surely and in $L^1(\mu)$ to $\int_R f\,d\mu$.
If $f$ is additionally bounded and Borel, then the continuous-time averages
$$\frac1{\tau}\int_0^\tau f(\Phi_s z)\,ds$$
converge $\mu$-almost surely and in $L^1(\mu)$ to the same mean as
$\tau\to\infty$. No ergodicity of every time map or generic Hamiltonian flow
is asserted.

references.title: David Tong, Classical Dynamics, complete author-hosted lecture notes, §4.2.3
Daniel Arovas, Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, §3.4
Rick Durrett, Probability: Theory and Examples, 5th ed., Theorem 6.2.1 and its complete proof

items.title: Mixing hierarchy for a selected probability-preserving map
items.statement:
For one fixed probability-preserving map $T$, strong mixing implies weak
mixing, and weak mixing implies ergodicity, under the exact definitions in
[[def-csm-dk-ergodic-and-mixing-notions]]. No converse is asserted.

references.title: E. H. El Abdalaoui and F. Vivaldi, Ergodic Theory and Dynamical Systems, §2.7
Peter Sarig, Lecture Notes on Ergodic Theory, Proposition 1.2

items.title: Liouville probability transport and constant fine entropy
items.statement:
Let $(M,\omega,H,\Phi,m_0)$ be a Hamiltonian phase datum and let $R\subseteq M$
be an open complete invariant domain. For any finite-valued Borel density
$\rho_0\ge0$ with $\rho_0\in L^1(m_0|_R)$ and
$\int_R\rho_0\,dm_0=1$, define
$\rho_t=\rho_0\circ\Phi_{-t}$. Then $\rho_t$ is a probability density for every
$t$, and for every bounded Borel observable $A$,
$$\int_R A\rho_t\,dm_0=\int_R(A\circ\Phi_t)\rho_0\,dm_0.$$
If $\rho_0$ is smooth, it satisfies the classical Liouville equation
$\partial_t\rho_t+X_H\rho_t=0$. For merely $L^1$ data, it satisfies the
distributional equation on $R$, meaning
$$\int_{\mathbb R}\int_R\rho_t (\partial_t\varphi+X_H\varphi)\,dm_0\,dt=0$$
for every smooth compactly supported test function
$\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R\times R)$.

If additionally $\int_R|\rho_0\log\rho_0|\,dm_0<\infty$, with
$0\log0=0$, then the reference-measure fine entropy
$$S_k(t)=-k\int_R\rho_t\log\rho_t\,dm_0,\qquad k>0,$$
is finite and constant. This is not a monotonicity claim for entropy after
coarse graining.

references.title: David Tong, Classical Dynamics, complete author-hosted lecture notes, §4.2.1
Daniel Arovas, Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, §3.2

items.title: Conditional Hamiltonian ensemble and response predictions
items.statement:
Adopt the selected smooth nonrelativistic Hamiltonian model and preparation
of [[post-csm-dk-selected-hamiltonian-dynamics]]. The following are
conditional model deductions, with no experimental premise.

1. If $\beta=(k_BT)^{-1}>0$ and
$Z_\beta=\int_R e^{-\beta H}\,dm_0$ is finite and positive, the canonical
probability $d\mu_\beta=Z_\beta^{-1}e^{-\beta H}dm_0$ is invariant under the
unforced Hamiltonian flow. For any absolutely continuous initial law covered
by [[thm-csm-dk-liouville-and-fine-entropy]], its Liouville-transported density
preserves the reference-measure fine entropy whenever that entropy is finite.

2. Under full AC, let $n\ge1$, let the canonical phase be open
$O\subseteq\mathbb R^{2n}$, let $H\in C^2(O,\mathbb R)$, and let
$J\subseteq\mathbb R$ be open. Suppose $\nabla H\ne0$ on $H^{-1}(J)$
and $H^{-1}(K)$ is compact in $O$ for every compact $K\subset J$. For
each $E\in J$ with nonempty shell $\Sigma_E=H^{-1}(\{E\})$, if the
flow preserves a full compact regular band containing $\Sigma_E$, that
shell has a finite positive
weighted area law invariant under that flow. Critical levels and noncompact
bands are outside this prediction.

3. If $\mu$ is a Borel probability on $R$ invariant under every flow map
$\Phi_s$ and the selected time map $T=\Phi_\Delta$ is ergodic for $\mu$
(every Borel $E$ with $T^{-1}E=E$ has $\mu(E)\in\{0,1\}$), then for each
bounded Borel observable $A$, the model's
continuous-time average of $A$ converges $\mu$-almost surely and in $L^1$
to its ensemble mean. This is a typical-initial-state prediction, not a
claim for every trajectory or every finite observation window.

4. In the compact response regime and with the unperturbed canonical
preparation, perturbing $H$ to $H-\epsilon h(t)B$ gives the exact
first-order response of [[thm-csm-dk-compact-hamiltonian-linear-response]].
It does not assert that the required correlation decays or that a
noncompact physical system satisfies the compact hypotheses.

In SI mechanical units, $H$ is in J, absolute temperature $T$ is in K,
$k_B$ is the adopted primitive energy-temperature conversion constant in
J/K, $\beta$ is in J$^{-1}$, and the action scale $a_0$ is in J s.
Observables and control fields retain the units declared in the response theorem. These
deductions establish what follows inside the adopted model, not that nature
obeys the model.

references.title: David Tong, Classical Dynamics, complete author-hosted lecture notes, §4.2
David Tong, Statistical Physics, complete author-hosted lecture text, §§1.2–1.3
Daniel Arovas, Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, §3.2
MIT OpenCourseWare, 22.103 Microscopic Theory of Transport, Lecture 3, pp. 1–4

items.title: Smooth state flow for continuous-time smooth-state force fields
items.design_state: Complete draft argument recorded; scoped checks and independent review remain pending.
items.statement:
Let $d\ge1$, let $I=[a,b]$ be a compact interval contained in an open interval $J\subseteq\mathbb R$, and let $G:J\times\mathbb T^d\to\mathbb R^d$ be continuous in time with jointly continuous state derivatives $D_x^rG$ on $J\times\mathbb T^d$ for every integer $r\ge1$. Assume that $G$ and each state derivative $D_x^rG$ are bounded on $I\times\mathbb T^d$ for every integer $r\ge1$. For initial data $(x_0,v_0)\in\mathbb T^d\times\mathbb R^d$, the system

$$\dot X(t)=V(t),\qquad \dot V(t)=G(t,X(t)),\qquad (X(a),V(a))=(x_0,v_0)$$

has a unique solution on all of $I$. For each $t\in I$, the map
$(x_0,v_0)\mapsto(X(t),V(t))$ is $C^\infty$; for every integer $r\ge1$ its
$r$th initial-state derivative is bounded uniformly over $t\in I$ and all
$(x_0,v_0)$. Its inverse is the solution map from $t$ back to $a$. If $G$ is
jointly $C^\infty$ in $(t,x)$ on $J\times\mathbb T^d$, then the flow is jointly
$C^\infty$ in time and initial state.
items.strategy: proof_strategy: direct; complete argument is in items/lem-csm-dk-continuous-time-field-smooth-flow.md and its proof contract.

references.title: Gerald Teschl, Ordinary Differential Equations and Dynamical Systems, Graduate Studies in Mathematics 140, American Mathematical Society (2012)
references.locator: Chapter 2 §§2.2, 2.4 and 2.6, printed pp. 36-53; Theorem 2.10 assumes joint C^k regularity in time and state, so the local proof below separately handles time-continuous fields with smooth state dependence.

items.title: Smooth periodic finite-N and scaled mean-field phase data
items.design_state: Draft definition carrier recorded; scoped checks and independent review remain pending.
items.statement:
Fix an integer $d\ge1$, a side length $L>0$ in metres, a mass $m>0$ in kilograms, and a smooth even periodic pair potential $W\in C^\infty(\mathbb T_L^d;\mathbb R)$ in joules, where $\mathbb T_L^d:=(\mathbb R/L\mathbb Z)^d$ is the flat position torus and even means $W(-q)=W(q)$. For each finite integer $N\ge1$, the phase space is $(T^*\mathbb T_L^d)^N$ with canonical coordinates $z_i=(q_i,p_i)$, $q_i\in\mathbb T_L^d$ in metres and $p_i\in\mathbb R^d$ in kilogram-metres per second. In position charts obtained by lifting torus coordinates to $\mathbb R^d$, define

$$\theta_N:=\sum_{i=1}^N\sum_{a=1}^d p_i^a\,dq_i^a,\qquad \omega_N:=-d\theta_N=\sum_{i=1}^N\sum_{a=1}^d dq_i^a\wedge dp_i^a.$$

Overlaps of these position charts are translations by vectors in $L\mathbb Z^d$, with the same momentum coordinates, so $dq_i^a$ and $p_i^a$ agree on overlaps. Thus the displayed forms glue globally on $(T^*\mathbb T_L^d)^N$; $\omega_N$ is closed and nondegenerate by its displayed coordinate matrix. Both forms have action units of joule-seconds. Use the Hamiltonian convention $\iota_{X_{H_N}}\omega_N=dH_N$ of [[def-csm-dk-hamiltonian-flow-measure]]. The finite-particle Hamiltonian, with energy in joules, is

$$H_N(q_1,\ldots,q_N,p_1,\ldots,p_N)=\sum_{i=1}^{N}\frac{|p_i|^2}{2m}+\frac1N\sum_{1\le i<j\le N}W(q_i-q_j).$$

The interaction force is $K(q):=-\nabla_qW(q)$, in newtons. It is bounded and globally Lipschitz on the compact torus; evenness of $W$ makes $K$ odd and $K(0)=0$. Hamilton's equations in the canonical convention are

$$\dot q_i=\frac{p_i}{m},\qquad \dot p_i=\frac1N\sum_{j\ne i}K(q_i-q_j).$$

For any chosen momentum scale $P_0>0$ in kilogram-metres per second, define the time scale $\tau_0:=mL/P_0$ in seconds, dimensionless variables $x_i:=q_i/L\in\mathbb T^d:=(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)^d$, $v_i:=p_i/P_0$, and $s:=t/\tau_0$. Define the dimensionless potential $\Phi(x):=mW(Lx)/P_0^2$ and force $k(x):=-\nabla_x\Phi(x)$. Then the equations become

$$x_i'=v_i,\qquad v_i'=\frac1N\sum_{j\ne i}k(x_i-x_j),$$

where prime denotes derivative with respect to dimensionless time $s$. Here
$\|Dk\|_\infty:=\sup_{x\in\mathbb T^d}\|Dk(x)\|_{\mathrm{op}}$, with operator
norm induced by the Euclidean norm, and $\|k\|_\infty:=\sup_x|k(x)|$; the
constants $A:=\|Dk\|_\infty$ and $B:=\|k\|_\infty$ are finite and
dimensionless. This is the selected smooth periodic mean-field scaling; it is
not the hard-sphere Boltzmann-Grad scaling.

references.title: François Golse, The Mean-Field Limit for the Dynamics of Large Particle Systems, Journées Équations aux dérivées partielles short course (2003), Sec. 1.1.1 and Part I

items.title: Wasserstein-1 coupling cost on dimensionless phase space
items.design_state: Draft definition carrier recorded; scoped checks and independent review remain pending.
items.statement:
Use the dimensionless one-particle phase space $Z:=\mathbb T^d\times\mathbb R^d$ from [[def-csm-dk-periodic-mean-field-model]], with its product topology and Borel sigma algebra. The finite torus is second-countable by [[def-the-one-dimensional-torus-and-normalized-haar-integral]], and Euclidean space is second-countable. Consequently $Z$ and $Z\times Z$ are second-countable, and the Borel sigma algebra of each finite product equals the product of the factor Borel sigma algebras: every open set is a countable union of basic open rectangles. Use the product topology and its Borel sigma algebra on $Z\times Z$ as well.

For $x,y\in\mathbb T^d$, let

$$d_{\mathbb T^d}(x,y):=\min_{\ell\in\mathbb Z^d}|\widetilde x-\widetilde y+\ell|,$$

where $\widetilde x,\widetilde y\in\mathbb R^d$ are any representatives; the minimum is independent of the representatives. Equip $Z$ with

$$d_Z((x,v),(y,w)):=d_{\mathbb T^d}(x,y)+|v-w|.$$

Let $\mathcal P_1(Z)$ be the Borel probability measures $\mu$ on $Z$ with $\int_Z|v|\,d\mu(x,v)<\infty$. For $\mu,\nu\in\mathcal P_1(Z)$, a coupling is a Borel probability $\pi$ on $Z\times Z$ satisfying $\pi(A\times Z)=\mu(A)$ and $\pi(Z\times B)=\nu(B)$ for all Borel $A,B\subseteq Z$; write $\Pi(\mu,\nu)$ for the set of couplings. Define the phase-space Wasserstein-1 coupling cost by

$$\mathcal W_1(\mu,\nu):=\inf_{\pi\in\Pi(\mu,\nu)}\int_{Z\times Z}d_Z(z,z')\,d\pi(z,z').$$

By [[thm-sigma-finite-product-measure-exists-is-rectangular-and-is-unique]], $\mu\otimes\nu$ is a probability on $\mathcal B(Z)\otimes\mathcal B(Z)=\mathcal B(Z\times Z)$ and its marginals are $\mu,\nu$; hence $\Pi(\mu,\nu)$ is nonempty. The infimum is finite: this product coupling has torus cost at most $\sqrt d/2$, and Tonelli's theorem bounds its velocity cost by $\int|v|\,d\mu+\int|w|\,d\nu$. No minimizing coupling is assumed to exist.

items.title: Selected mean-field particle model and iid preparation
items.design_state: Draft postulate carrier recorded; scoped checks and independent review remain pending.
items.statement:
Adopt [[def-csm-dk-periodic-mean-field-model]] as the selected finite-particle model: for each $N\ge1$, the phase points $(q_i,p_i)$ evolve by its displayed Hamilton equations with smooth even periodic potential $W$ and interaction coefficient $1/N$. This is a model assumption with $q_i$ in metres, $p_i$ in kilogram-metres per second, $m$ in kilograms, $W$ in joules, and force $K=-\nabla W$ in newtons.

For the propagation-of-chaos preparation branch, give $Z=\mathbb T^d\times\mathbb R^d$ its product topology and the Borel sigma algebra generated by its open sets. Choose a Borel probability $\mu_0$ and a compact set $K\subset Z$ with $\mu_0(K)=1$. Put $\Omega=Z^{\mathbb N}$ with product sigma algebra $\mathcal B(Z)^{\otimes\mathbb N}$. Under the full Axiom of Choice, [[thm-ionescu-tulcea-construction-of-a-markov-chain]] applied to the constant kernels $K_n(z_0,\ldots,z_n,A)=\mu_0(A)$ supplies a probability $P$ on $\Omega$. Let $Z_i(0):\Omega\to Z$ be the coordinate projections, and use the first $N$ coordinates for the finite-$N$ preparation. For every finite list of indices $i_1<\cdots<i_r$ and Borel sets $A_1,\ldots,A_r\subseteq Z$, this construction gives

$$P\bigl(Z_{i_1}(0)\in A_1,\ldots,Z_{i_r}(0)\in A_r\bigr)=\prod_{j=1}^r\mu_0(A_j).$$

Thus each coordinate has law $\mu_0$ and the coordinates are mutually independent. Here “iid” means exactly this common-marginal and finite-rectangle factorization property. The cited construction uses Choice to choose a compatible infinite coordinate sequence and again to choose successive coordinates in its continuity-at-the-empty-set argument; this postulate does not weaken that assumption.

These assumptions define the selected physical model and preparation. They do not assert that a real gas, hard-sphere system, or experiment realizes them, and they do not deduce the assumptions from mechanics or observation.

items.title: Complete finite-N flow and permutation-invariant Liouville law
items.design_state: Complete draft argument recorded; scoped checks and independent review remain pending.
items.statement:
Assume countable choice [[def-countable-choice]] for the intrinsic
density-measure construction in [[def-csm-dk-hamiltonian-flow-measure]]. On
$(T^*\mathbb T_L^d)^N$, use the canonical form
$\omega_N:=\sum_{i=1}^N\sum_{a=1}^d dq_i^a\wedge dp_{i,a}$ and Liouville
volume form $\Omega_N:=\omega_N^{dN}/(dN)!$. The positive reference density
$|\Omega_N|/a_0^{dN}$ induces a Borel measure $m_{0,N}$ by that definition;
write $d\Omega_N:=a_0^{dN}dm_{0,N}$ for canonical Liouville measure, which
in canonical coordinates is $dq_1\,dp_1\cdots dq_N\,dp_N$. Fix $d\ge1$,
$m,L>0$, a finite integer $N\ge1$, and the periodic smooth even potential
and canonical phase-space convention of
[[def-csm-dk-periodic-mean-field-model]]. The associated Hamiltonian ODE has
a unique complete smooth flow $\Phi_t^N$ on $(T^*\mathbb T_L^d)^N$ for all
$t\in\mathbb R$. It preserves $\Omega_N$ and commutes with permutations of
the $N$ particle labels.

If the initial law has a normalized symmetric $C^\infty$ density
$F_N^0(q_1,\ldots,q_N,p_1,\ldots,p_N)$ relative to $d\Omega_N$ and, for
every pair of multi-indices $\alpha,\beta$ and integer $r\ge0$,

$$\sup_{q\in(\mathbb T_L^d)^N,\ p\in\mathbb R^{dN}}(1+|p|)^r|\partial_q^\alpha\partial_p^\beta F_N^0(q,p)|<\infty,$$

then $F_N(t):=F_N^0\circ\Phi_{-t}^N$ is a normalized symmetric classical solution of the Liouville equation for all $t$. Its momentum tails, together with every phase derivative, remain rapidly decreasing uniformly on each bounded time interval.
items.strategy: proof_strategy: direct; complete argument is in items/thm-csm-dk-finite-n-complete-flow.md and its proof contract.

items.title: Exact normalized BBGKY hierarchy
items.design_state: Complete draft argument recorded; scoped checks and independent review remain pending.
items.statement:
Fix the smooth periodic finite-N model and complete flow $\Phi_t^N$ of [[thm-csm-dk-finite-n-complete-flow]]. Let $F_N(t)=F_N^0\circ\Phi_{-t}^N$ be the transported normalized symmetric $C^\infty$ probability density relative to canonical phase volume, with all phase derivatives rapidly decreasing in momentum uniformly in position on each finite time slab. Here $z_i=(q_i,p_i)$, and rapid decrease means that for every position multi-index $\alpha$, momentum multi-index $\beta$, and integer $r\ge0$, $(1+|p|)^r|\partial_q^\alpha\partial_p^\beta F_N(t,q,p)|$ is uniformly bounded on that slab. For $1\le k\le N$, define the normalized marginal

$$f_k(t,z_1,\ldots,z_k):=\int F_N(t,z_1,\ldots,z_N)\,dz_{k+1}\cdots dz_N.$$

Then, for $1\le k\le N$,

$$\partial_t f_k+\sum_{i=1}^k\frac{p_i}{m}\cdot\nabla_{q_i}f_k+\frac1N\sum_{1\le i<j\le k}K(q_i-q_j)\cdot(\nabla_{p_i}-\nabla_{p_j})f_k+\frac{N-k}{N}\sum_{i=1}^k\nabla_{p_i}\cdot\int K(q_i-q_{k+1})f_{k+1}(t,z_1,\ldots,z_{k+1})\,dz_{k+1}=0.$$

When $k=N$, the last term is zero and no $f_{N+1}$ is used. This identity is exact at finite $N$ and makes no factorization or molecular-chaos assumption.
items.strategy: proof_strategy: direct; complete argument is in items/thm-csm-dk-exact-bbgky.md and its proof contract.

items.title: Smooth compact tests determine phase-space probabilities
items.design_state: Complete draft argument recorded; scoped checks and independent review remain pending.
items.statement:
Use $Z=\mathbb T^d\times\mathbb R^d$ and
$d_Z((x,v),(y,w))=d_{\mathbb T^d}(x,y)+|v-w|$ from
[[def-csm-dk-phase-space-wasserstein-one]]. Let $\mu$ and $\nu$ be Borel
probability measures on $Z$. If

$$\int_Z\varphi\,d\mu=\int_Z\varphi\,d\nu \quad\text{for every }\varphi\in C_c^\infty(Z),$$

where $C_c^\infty(Z)$ means smooth and periodic in position with compact
velocity support, then $\mu=\nu$ on all Borel subsets of $Z$.

items.title: Complete global bounded-Lipschitz mean-field characteristic evolution
items.design_state: Complete draft argument recorded; scoped checks and independent review remain pending.
items.statement:
Let $Z=\mathbb T^d\times\mathbb R^d$ be the dimensionless phase space from
[[def-csm-dk-periodic-mean-field-model]], let $k$ be the odd, bounded, smooth,
Lipschitz force in that definition, and put $B=\|k\|_\infty$ and
$A=\|Dk\|_\infty$ using its stated operator norm. Let $\mu_0$ be any Borel
probability on $Z$ with finite first velocity moment
$\int_Z|v|\,d\mu_0(x,v)$. Then there is a unique global characteristic
evolution $(X_s,V_s)$ with

$$\dot X_s(z)=V_s(z),\qquad \dot V_s(z)=\int_Z k(X_s(z)-X_s(z'))\,d\mu_0(z'),\qquad (X_0,V_0)(x,v)=(x,v),$$

and $\mu_s$ is the push-forward of $\mu_0$ by $S_s(z):=(X_s(z),V_s(z))$; here
the push-forward is defined by $\mu_s(A)=\mu_0(S_s^{-1}(A))$ for each Borel set
$A\subseteq Z$. It is narrowly continuous with finite first velocity moment for every $s\in\mathbb R$. It
satisfies the weak Vlasov equation: for every time-dependent $C^1$ function
$\varphi(s,x,v)$ that is bounded with bounded first derivatives and periodic
in $x$,

$$\frac{d}{ds}\int_Z\varphi(s,z)\,d\mu_s(z) =\int_Z\bigl(\partial_s\varphi+v\cdot\nabla_x\varphi +F_{\mu_s}(x)\cdot\nabla_v\varphi\bigr)(s,z)\,d\mu_s(z),\qquad F_{\mu_s}(x):=\int_Z k(x-y)\,d\mu_s(y,w).$$

For the density clause, use $dx=m_{\mathbb T^d}$ and $dv=\lambda_d$, the
normalized torus probability and Euclidean Lebesgue measure defined in
[[def-the-one-dimensional-torus-and-normalized-haar-integral]]. If $\mu_0$ has a smooth probability
density $\rho_0$ with respect to $dx\,dv$ and all velocity moments
$\int_Z(1+|v|^r)\rho_0(x,v)\,dx\,dv$ are finite for integers $r\ge1$, then
$F_{\mu_s}$ is jointly smooth in $(s,x)$ and the transported density is a
classical smooth solution of this Vlasov equation.
items.strategy: proof_strategy: direct; complete argument is in items/thm-csm-dk-global-lipschitz-vlasov.md and its proof contract.
